newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SM SUMMIT SHARES UP AS SUSPENSION LIFTED.
newsitem.headline: SM SUMMIT SHARES UP AS SUSPENSION LIFTED.

text.p: Shares in compact disc-maker SM Summit Holdings Ltd rallied 8.5 cents to a high of Singapore $0.74 on Thursday after trading in its shares was allowed to resume following a half-day suspension.

The shares were suspended on Wednesday after they fell almost 38 percent to a low of S$0.655 after news that the company's offices had been raided by police and industry officials on suspicion of illegal software manufacture.
SM Summit and one other local company face civil suits from U.S. giant Microsoft Corp and two other U.S. software companies.
But SM Summit denies all the charges against it and has said it will defend itself and take all necessary steps to guard its interests.
SM Summit shares were at S$0.715 at 0115 GMT, up six cents.
